problem: Fine-tune a pretrained flow-based VLA without repeatedly executing every policy update on physical hardware.
contribution: VLA-RFT combines an action-conditioned autoregressive world simulator, stochastic flow-policy parameterization and group-relative optimization. Its 'verified' reward means reference-trajectory similarity, not independent verification of real task completion.
algorithm: Pretrain a compact video tokenizer/138M LLaMA-style transition model and a VLA-Adapter policy offline. Add a learned Sigma Net to the flow head and sample Gaussian denoising transitions over ten Euler steps. Compare generated trajectories with reference trajectories using weighted L1 and LPIPS; group-center rewards and update flow/sigma parameters with clipped ratios, entropy and auxiliary flow-matching supervision. Final reward design compares both policy and reference actions rendered by the same model.
observations: Initial image, language and proprioception; offline labeled action/image sequences. World model recursively predicts RGB conditioned on action history. Reward requires reference expert actions/frames; generated visual fidelity alone does not establish force/contact accuracy.
actions: Seven-dimensional actions matching the training dataset and action chunks. Stochastic flow denoising likelihood is used during optimization; it does not define a calibrated target-robot interface.
embodiment_and_data: LIBERO four simulated suites; model and policy both pretrained on task datasets. Experiments use four A800 GPUs. No physical robot evaluation is established in the inspected experiments.
experiments: Compare150k-step supervised base with400 RFT iterations, standard suite success and object/goal/robot-state perturbations. Reward ablations compare direct action similarity, generated-versus-real images, and generated-versus-generated reference. WM metrics include MSE/PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS rather than physical validity tests.
baselines: Base supervised VLA at30k and150k iterations; three reward definitions. This is chiefly a within-policy post-training comparison rather than a broad matched-budget physical RL benchmark.
quantitative_result: Table2 PDFp8 gives86.6% base versus91.1% RFT, +4.5 percentage points after400 iterations. Adjacent prose p7 says91.3%/+4.7, inconsistent with the table and Table4p9; retain table value and flag discrepancy. Table4:action-only87.7%, direct image comparison87.1%, generated-reference91.1%. Table3p9 combined major perturbation34.0→37.0%, far below standard-suite average.
limitations: Expert-similarity rewards constrain discovery beyond expert quality and can favor visually similar behavior. Learned-model capacity/support limits OOD reliability; model-based planning is not included. Reward is not independent of the simulator. Simulated task improvement does not establish physical force or grasp correctness; table/prose numerical inconsistency remains unresolved.
code_and_license: Code, checkpoint and dataset license texts were not independently inspected; public paper availability is not a code/model license. No code inspected or executed.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE as a simulation-only post-training baseline after action schema and reference trajectories exist. Do not label imitation-distance reward as validated physical success; independently score real outcomes and model errors before applying policies to SO101/ROSMASTER. No controller changes implied.
